children: The Indian rupee started the session with marginal losses against the US dollar on September 9, weighed down by a further rise in oil prices, which would test the central bank's ability to cushion the currency.
The rupee opened almost flat at 94.87 per dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 94.82.
According to Finrex, the rupee is expected to open around 94.85 per dollar and trade in the 94.50-95.25 range, with Brent crude holding near $99.25 a barrel.

Importers are expected to buy on dips, while exporters may step in to sell above 95.00. The RBI's intervention will be closely watched, with the central bank potentially helping protect the 95.00 per dollar level during the session, it added.

Asian currencies were mostly higher against the US dollar, with the Malaysian ringgit the only currency to weaken. The Philippines peso recorded the strongest gain at 0.188%, followed by the Japanese yen at 0.182%.
The Thai baht rose 0.085%, while the South Korean won gained 0.064%. The Singapore dollar and Indonesian rupiah strengthened 0.055% and 0.045%, respectively.
The Taiwan dollar and Chinese renminbi also edged higher by 0.038% and 0.028%.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens marginally lower at 94.87 per dollar; Asian currencies gain
